title: Arjuna meets his son in battle
hook: the sacrificial horse reaches Manipura, and the young king who comes out to meet Arjuna is his own son
carry: svadharma: do the duty of the role you're in
tomorrow: the great sacrifice is done. why is a half-golden mongoose unimpressed?

segments.voice: Yesterday, in the Ashvamedhika, a child born without breath lived, by Krishna's declaration of truth. His name is Parikshit. Your line was satya: a truthful life gives a promise power.

The horse has been set loose at last. It wanders where it likes, and Arjuna follows with his bow, country after country, fighting the kings who challenge it. Then it walks into Manipura. Long ago, on his travels, Arjuna married a princess of this land, Chitrangada, and left a son here. That son, Babhruvahana, is king now. And he comes out of the city to meet the horse, not with an army but with gifts and brahmanas, his head bowed to his father.
screen: `THE HORSE WANDERS.` → `IT ENTERS MANIPURA.` → `HIS SON COMES OUT WITH GIFTS.`

segments.voice: Arjuna is angry. In Ganguli's telling he scolds his son: I've come as a warrior guarding a sacrificial horse, and you greet me like this? A king of your order should fight. Then someone rises out of the earth: Ulupi, the serpent princess, another of Arjuna's wives. Do what your father asks, she tells the young king. Fight him. So father and son meet in battle, and the son is very good. His arrow strikes Arjuna, and Arjuna falls and does not get up. Then Ulupi places a gem from the serpent world on Arjuna's chest, and he wakes as if from sleep. She explains: when Arjuna brought Bhishma down from behind Shikhandi, the Vasus, Bhishma's divine brothers, cursed him, and the curse was to end at his own son's hands. Today it did. Now the teaching underneath. Hindus call it svadharma, your own duty, and it changes with the role you're standing in. As a son, Babhruvahana bows. As the king whose land the horse has entered, he must ride out. Arjuna knows this from the inside. Before the war he begged not to fight his own grandfather and teacher, and Krishna told him in the Gita: better your own dharma, done imperfectly, than another's done well. Now the student of the Gita says it to his son. Many teachers read the scene as the Gita coming home, and the duty done fully is what frees Arjuna.
screen: `ARJUNA: "A KING SHOULD FIGHT"` · `THE SON'S ARROW FELLS THE FATHER` · `A GEM, AND AN OLD CURSE LIFTED` · `BOW AS SON, RIDE AS KING` · then, large: `SVADHARMA: THE DUTY OF YOUR ROLE`

segments.voice: Put your palms together and picture a parent or an elder in front of you. Bow to them a little, the way Babhruvahana bowed and the way many Hindus greet an elder with pranam, touching their feet. Then name one role you'll stand in today, where you may have to speak up or hold your ground, even with someone you respect. If you pray, ask for the strength to do that duty well; if you don't, just hold both, the bow and the duty.
Ashvamedhika. The book where a father, following the horse, is struck down by his own son and brought back by a serpent princess's gem.
Your line: svadharma, do the duty of the role you're in. The son's arrow ended the father's curse. Day eight hundred seventy-one.

howItsDone: Arjuna's encounter with Babhruvahana is told in the Ashvamedhika Parva and retold in Indian theater and storytelling; teachers often set it beside Krishna's call to svadharma in the Gita.

fork.setup: you're Babhruvahana. as a son you bowed. now your father says the king of this land should meet the horse's guardian in battle. by svadharma, what fits?
options: fight him: as king, defending your land is your duty today.
keep bowing: a son's duty always comes first.
hand the fight to your generals.
fork.reveal: Babhruvahana bowed as a son, then fought as a king when Arjuna named that his duty, and his arrow ended the Vasus' curse. svadharma: each role asks its own duty.

original.note: Ulupi: the serpent princess, Arjuna's wife, who urges the fight and revives him.

chat.meaning: Babhruvahana bowed to Arjuna as a son, then fought him as a king when Arjuna said that was his duty. Hindus call it svadharma: each role has its own duty.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm Arjuna's rebuke of Babhruvahana and Ulupi's emergence from the earth as Ganguli tells it.
Confirm the curse: the Vasus cursed Arjuna for felling Bhishma with Shikhandi before him, Ulupi's father interceded, and the curse was to end at his son's hands.
The gem is called the Sanjivana gem in some tellings; the name is left out pending confirmation.
